findings.text: A huge table sharing teardown interface reports whether a middle directory entry was unshared and provides a companion flush operation. One configuration performs size and sharing checks with mapping and area lock validation before clearing and accounting, while an alternate configuration is inert and always reports no work and does nothing on flush.

A size dependent mask helper returns a span derived from upper table sizes for the largest huge sizes and an empty result for other sizes. A weak variant preserves only the middle level span under sharing support and otherwise returns an empty result.

Transparent huge PUD teardown is exposed through a zap routine returning handled status and a lock acquisition helper returning a spin lock only for huge entries and a reverse mapping removal helper that is active only with huge PUD support.

Global reservation helpers expose a private lock predicate for non shared areas and an assertion that validates the appropriate area or map semaphore is held and a file region uncharge routine that scales by pages per huge page and conditionally releases control group references.

For huge page areas the private pointer carries both a reservation map address and flag bits. Flag updates preserve the address by logical combination and flag tests mask with the relevant owner or mask constants and the area is expected to be huge and non shared where private flags are manipulated.

The reservation map source depends on sharing mode. Shared areas use the map belonging to the host inode reached through the file mapping, while private areas extract the map address from the private pointer after clearing flag bits. Missing maps are treated as needing reservation.
Reservation accounting indexes a fault address by converting it to a linear page index within the area and shifting by the huge page order of the associated state.

Shared and private reservation maps have opposite presence meaning. Presence in a shared map denotes reserved capacity, while absence in a private map denotes remaining reservation and presence denotes consumed reservation, so private results are inverted. Private reservations are normally present but may disappear after hole punch or truncation of the backing file.

Single page reservation probes and updates assume at most a single new region descriptor is required and that single page commits never fail for lack of descriptors. Cache allocation is asserted unnecessary for unit ranges.

Region descriptor caching tracks available entries and in progress additions. Probes reserve capacity for the estimated need with a minimum of a single entry and commits consume the prior reservation and aborts release it. Growth ensures capacity covers in progress work plus new need before proceeding, retrying if the map changed concurrently.

Reservation insertion fills only uncovered gaps within the requested interval and reports covered length. Newly inserted extents merge with contiguous neighbors only when boundaries meet exactly and control group uncharge identity matches, with absorbed entries freed and their references released.

When control group accounting is enabled, each new region records a per size reservation counter and a referenced control group pointer, with a uniform pages per huge page value enforced per map. Split regions duplicate the identity with an additional reference and removal scales uncharge by that factor and the control reference is released only when an entire region disappears.

Address range teardown walks upper page table levels by advancing to per level boundaries, skipping absent or invalid entries and descending otherwise. Partial huge PUD entries are split and whole ones are zapped directly without descent and traversal yields the processor periodically. Special huge areas bypass page accounting, while anonymous or non present huge PUD entries are treated as unexpected.
Special huge treatment applies to areas marked as direct physical or mixed mapping, excluding direct access file mappings.
Unsharing applies only to middle directory sized huge pages whose table descriptor is marked shared. Other sizes or non shared tables complete successfully without action.

Reservation range mutation and accounting are serialized by a per map spin lock. Probes, commits and aborts hold it while updating counts and deletion holds it while scanning and trimming and cache growth temporarily releases it for allocation then reacquires and revalidates before continuing.

Huge PUD teardown serializes on the PUD spin lock. The lock is retained only when the entry is confirmed huge under the lock and otherwise it is released and no teardown occurs. Clearing and accounting occur under that lock with release before reclaim queuing.

Page table unsharing and its flush require the file mapping lock held for writing. Unsharing additionally validates that the appropriate area lock is held, dispatching to a per area semaphore for shareable locks or a reservation map semaphore for private reservation owners.

A reservation map aggregates an ordered extent list and a cache list with a count of available descriptors and a count of in progress additions and a spin lock and a read write semaphore, plus accounting fields for pages per huge page and an optional aggregate reservation counter.

A reservation extent carries inclusive start and exclusive end offsets in huge page units with list linkage and optional control group uncharge identity consisting of a counter pointer and a subsystem pointer. A degenerate zero length form may appear as a placeholder at deletion boundaries.

Huge reservation state links a virtual area through its flags and private pointer and file mapping and memory descriptor to either a per area map or an inode hosted map. Shared selection traverses file to mapping to host inode to its map and private selection decodes the map from the private pointer.

Reservation updates dispatch on five modes. Need probes uncovered length and commit records presence and end releases a probe, while add and delete have mirrored shared versus private effects. Shared add records and shared delete removes and private add removes a consumption marker and private delete records one. Shared outcomes and private delete outcomes are returned directly and other private outcomes are inverted.

Interval deletion scans extents in order and applies one action per overlap. It skips non overlapping prefixes including placeholder handling and splits a strictly enclosing extent with a newly sourced descriptor and removes fully covered extents and trims a partially overlapped head or tail while accounting the removed length and uncharging accordingly.

Range insertion scans extents in order, advancing a last accounted cursor over overlapping prefixes and stopping before the first extent starting at or beyond the range end and filling each gap between cursor and next start and finally filling any tail beyond the last overlapping extent.

Two thin wrappers translate a fault address to a huge cache index and delegate to common reservation logic for need probing and for addition respectively, returning a positive indicator when no map exists.

Upper level zap helpers serve as teardown entries that iterate one table level and delegate each present child to the next lower level, with the PUD level integrating huge page splitting and direct huge reclamation before descent.

Failure and diagnostic paths include out of memory when growing descriptor caches or splitting extents and fatal handling for unknown reservation modes and assertions for cache and accounting consistency and huge area expectations and warnings for anonymous or non present huge PUD pages and for reverse mapping removal without PUD huge support.

Reservation and teardown behaviour keys on named constants whose values are not shown here. Flag isolation uses HPAGE_RESV_MASK with ownership indicated by HPAGE_RESV_OWNER and sharing selected by VM_MAYSHARE. Span and eligibility checks use PMD_SIZE alongside PUD_SIZE alongside P4D_SIZE. PUD reclamation accounting uses HPAGE_PUD_SIZE alongside HPAGE_PUD_NR.
